approachQuestion.prompt:
A static bitmap is packed into m W-bit words. Within each word, the lowest bit represents the earliest position. For each of q queries p, return the number of set bits among positions 0 through p-1; p=0 asks about the empty prefix.

Constraints: 1 <= W <= 64; 1 <= m,q <= 200000; 0 <= p <= mW.
Example: W=4, words=[11,4], queries=[0,3,4,8] -> [0,2,3,4].

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: W is a parameter. W-bit popcount, shifts and masks cost constant time. Counters/indices fit in machine words large enough for mW and q. Query results occupy the returned q-entry array.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Build counts for prefixes of whole words. For query p, use b=floor(p/W) and r=p mod W: add prefix[b] to the popcount of the lowest r bits of word b; when r=0, add zero without reading word b.
options.feedback: The prefix splits into complete words and one partial word. The r=0 case also handles p=mW without an out-of-range access.

options.text: For each query, scan its complete words and count the low bits of its final partial word, without preprocessing.
options.feedback: It returns the right count for all boundaries, but repeats full-word work across queries.

options.text: Unpack all mW bits and build a cumulative count for every bit position; answer queries from that array.
options.feedback: This is correct but expands each word into W stored positions, which the packed prefix method avoids.

options.text: Return the total count through the entire word containing the last queried bit, ignoring the exact partial-word boundary.
options.feedback: For W=4, words=[11], p=1, this returns 3 instead of 1.

feedback.reason: Whole-word prefixes account for complete words before a query boundary.
details: Precompute one count per whole-word prefix, starting with zero. A query uses that count and at most one masked popcount on the trailing partial word. Skip that read when the remainder is zero, including the end-of-bitmap query.

Whole-word prefixes account for complete words before a query boundary. Mask and popcount only the final partial word. A boundary exactly at a word end must not read the next word, especially at bitmap end.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For prefix-whole-word-counts, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let m be the payload word count and q the query count. W remains a parameter.
constraints: W is a parameter. W-bit popcount, shifts and masks cost constant time. Counters/indices fit in machine words large enough for mW and q. Query results occupy the returned q-entry array.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Build m+1 counters and answer q queries with fixed word work.
details: Whole-word prefix construction visits m words and creates m+1 counters. Each query uses fixed word work. The q result entries are output and excluded; no unpacked bitmap or recursive stack is used.
W is a parameter. W-bit popcount, shifts and masks cost constant time. Counters/indices fit in machine words large enough for mW and q. Query results occupy the returned q-entry array.
“O(mq) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: That describes scanning each query prefix rather than storing a whole-word prefix array.
“O(mW+q) time, O(mW) auxiliary space”: This describes expanding to per-bit prefixes.
“O(q) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This omits preprocessing and its retained count array.
